speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing weakness and fatigue; to begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any associated fever, weight changes, or changes in your bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: 33-year-old woman. The patient reports feeling extremely fatigued and weak, especially towards the end of the day, to the point of difficulty in self-care. She mentions experiencing these symptoms currently. The patient has been traveling, hiking, and camping recently and notes having had multiple illnesses in the recent past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent travel, hiking, and camping, have you noticed any specific environmental exposures like tick bites, contaminated water, or insect stings? Additionally, has anyone around you become ill recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness and fatigue. I also have Mild diplopia.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of progressive weakness, fatigue, and new-onset mild diplopia (double vision) is highly suggestive of neuromuscular junction pathology, specifically Myasthenia Gravis. Please confirm if your fatigue worsens significantly with activity and improves with rest, and REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies (AChR-Ab).
